title: Bias Patterns in the Application of LLMs for Clinical Decision Support: A Comprehensive Study.
summary: The journal version reports bias patterns across eight LLMs and clinical-vignette tasks; an earlier arXiv version reported the same study, and the journal version adds an author and expanded analyses. The findings are task- and prompt-specific and do not establish bias across all clinical use. AI role: eight general-purpose and clinically trained LLMs evaluated across three standardized question-answering datasets using demographic red-teaming and prompt comparisons. The later peer-reviewed journal version appeared in Delaware Journal of Public Health in 2026.
ai_technology: Eight large language models tested on clinical vignettes

evidence.tested: Primary journal and earlier arXiv version study bias patterns in eight LLMs across clinical vignette tasks. Journal version adds a coauthor and expanded analyses; both are one study.
evidence.unknown: The results depend on the selected eight models, three vignette datasets, demographic attributes, prompts, and scoring; clinical outcomes and model behavior in deployed care were not evaluated. The arXiv and journal versions are one study.
evidence.ai_role: Eight large language models tested on clinical vignettes

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
